# Native Activation Manifold and Complete-State Replay (Provisional)

## Admitted Physical System

F05e (#11958, parent F05 #11789) admits only a self-contained MuJoCo 3.8.0
Euler XML fixture with one floating root, hinge/slide joints, built-in
joint-driven muscles, bounded dimensionless commands, and no collision,
equality constraint, tendon, plugin, callback, external load, or asset
dependency. The synthetic fixture has $n_q=8$, $n_v=7$, $n_a=n_u=1$ and
$h=0.001\,\mathrm{s}$. Its root is unactuated. Neither its geometry nor
its force law represents a golfer or measured motion.

## State, Dynamics, and Numerical Policy

The Crocoddyl physical state is $x=(q,v,a)$, with
$n_x=n_q+n_v+n_a=16$ and tangent dimension
$n_{\delta x}=2n_v+n_a=15$. MuJoCo's `mj_differentiatePos` and
`mj_integratePos` define the configuration difference and retraction;
activation difference is Euclidean within its admitted interior. No
activation clipping is hidden in retraction. The complete
`mjSTATE_INTEGRATION` payload has 50 values in this fixture and is carried
**separately** as the native restart and replay state. It is not inserted
into the optimizer manifold with zero-difference numerical axes.

The admitted model disables MuJoCo warmstart and automatic reset, and the
compiled-model/policy identity is bound to the native provider. Active
constraints, joint-limit boundary crossings, unsupported callbacks and
source assets reject before derivatives. For this narrow fixture,
two different warmstart histories and clocks with the same physical
state and command yield the same next physical state in the recorded test.
That test is a local numerical-history check, not a general Markov proof
for contacting or time-dependent models.

Each action advances the actual native Euler map
$x_{k+1}=F_h(x_k,u_k)$ and obtains its local tangent matrices through
`mjd_transitionFD`, including activation sensitivity:

$$
\delta x_{k+1}\simeq A_k\delta x_k+B_k\delta u_k,
\qquad
A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{15\times15},\quad
B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{15\times1}.
$$

Independent native centered directions at two interior perturbation sizes,
quaternion sign/retraction identities, and seeded Crocoddyl state Jacobian
checks exercise this boundary. The source-hashed diagnostic receipt records
the actual errors and dimensions. It does not run or select an optimizer.

The activation and direct-motor manifold adapters share
`native_manifold_calculus.py` for difference/retraction Jacobians and quadratic
tracking derivatives. Their model-specific state validation and native dynamics
remain at each adapter boundary. Tracking curvature is Gauss–Newton: it omits
second derivatives of the composed residual, including the native step and
manifold difference. The activation adapter identity binds
both its own source and the shared calculus bytes; a changed helper rejects
replay against the previous identity. This source closure is separate from the
self-contained model XML closure.

## Frozen Command Replay and Limits

The command is a compiled actuator control in unit `1`. It is not a joint
torque, realized muscle force, or an excitation-only channel contract.
The provider binds ordered channel IDs, native compiled law, source XML,
loaded model, and adapter identities. After uninterrupted native execution,
the actual held commands and complete initial integration state enter a
pinned Tools T01 `ExperimentReplayBundle` with a time-only, zero-order-held
policy. A fresh model reloads the bundle and independently reproduces all
complete native state rows. Input clocks and state identities are distinct;
there is no observation feedback in replay.

The test fixture's native derivative and three-step replay are software
boundary evidence only. No active contact or joint-limit regime, mixed
motor/muscle production model, private capture, anatomical validity, hard
real-time budget, full-swing tracking, six-engine comparison, or F05 solver
selection is qualified. The compiled-command comparison profile remains
pending its separate Tools/F01/F09 admission path. F05 and manual
publication remain blocked.
